name: Candy Mountain

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Chardonnay, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay and Merlot sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Riesling is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.

soil.rock: Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it. Loess is fine, wind-blown silt. Fertile and warm, it holds water well but drains poorly. Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium.
soil.top: The topsoil holds plenty of water, which can push leafy, vigorous vines unless growers rein them in. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
